The report says over 500 prisoners were taken and sent to the rear; how many were set to this work, with what tools and where the graves were is not stated. window.part_of_day: during the fight, about 4 to 8 p. m.

quote: I sent four of them, one after another, with orders for ammunition. The ammunition came promptly, was distributed at once, and the fight went on.

notes: Colonel Chamberlain and other commanders said their commands were out of ammunition; Rice sent four officers "pressed into service" for it; it came "promptly" and "was distributed at once". Who carried it and in what, and how much, is not stated. Barnes (OR27-1-R189) says the 20th Maine "replenished it from the cartridgeboxes of the men lying around them".

window.note: the supplementary report has the brigade on the field "until about 9 a. m., when we were relieved by the First Brigade and Ninth Massachusetts"; "the balance of the day" in reserve: the end is the day bound

context_quote: Remained on the field of the previous day's fight until about 9 a. m., when we were relieved by the First Brigade and Ninth Massachusetts, of the Second Brigade
notes: (The print has "tb" for "to".) The brigade lay in reserve during the cannonade of 3 July "with no loss, from the security of its position". The main report says the center of the line; the supplementary report says "we taking their old position farther to the right" (the Second Brigade's): the two wordings may describe the same ground.

Massed at first with the rest of the division on the right of the road, we were moved several times farther toward the left. Although expecting every moment to be put into action and held strictly in line of battle, yet the men were able to take some rest and make the most of their rations. Somewhere near 4 p. m. a sharp cannonade

tools_props.item: head-boards made of ammunition boxes with the soldier's name cut upon each

Rice (OR27-1-R195) says prisoners buried the brigade's dead on the morning of 3 July; Barnes says the Third Brigade spent 3 July in burying the dead (conflict C-LRT-BURIAL).

window.part_of_day: massed in the woods from 10 a. m. on the 3d to noon on the 4th
window.note: "until 10 a. m." on the 3d, then massed "Here I remained until 13 m., the 4th": the print has "13 m." (a clock time that does not exist), read as 12 m. (noon)

place.text: massed in the woods just at the right of General Sykes' headquarters

tier_basis: "13 m., the 4th" cannot be a clock time; it is read as 12 m. by the 2-for-3 confusion of this print (the same itinerary prints "13 m." in the 83rd Pennsylvania's own report R202 where Rice's report R195 prints "12 m." for the 6 July entry); the 10 a. m. is read as printed. Where the report says the regiment massed and "remained" it does not say what the men did.
quote: Remained here until 10 a. m., when, being relieved by a regiment of the Pennsylvania Reserves, rejoined my brigade, massed in the woods, just at the right of General Sykes' headquarters. Here I remained until 13 m., the 4th, when the brigade was thrown forward on a reconnaissance.
notes: The relief on the morning of 3 July is by "a regiment of the Pennsylvania Reserves" here, by the First Brigade and the Ninth Massachusetts in Lamont's itinerary (9 a. m.) and by Colonel Hayes's 18th Massachusetts in Conner's report (8 a. m.): conflict C-RELIEF-0703.

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

window.part_of_day: encamped at 7 p. m.
window.note: "encamped at 7 p. m." (the print is clear: Rice's report has "7 a. m. [p. m.]"); the next entry has the camp left at 4 a. m. on the 30th

place.text: 2 miles beyond Liberty, Md., on the road toward Johnsville

tier_basis: The print has "June 89" for the date; the entries run "Jwne 38" (28 June), "June 89", "June 30": the date is read as 29 June from the sequence and from the same entry in Rice's itinerary (R195).
quote: June 89. — Left camp in the morning, and marched 2 miles beyond Liberty, in the direction of Johns ville; encamped at 7 p. m.
notes: Second statement of the 29 June camp (Rice, brigade): this one reads "7 p. m.".

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

window.part_of_day: at Hanover, about 3 to 5 p. m.

place.text: Hanover, Pa.

quote: arriving at Hanover at about .3 p. m. ; left again at 5 o'clock
context_quote: July 1. — Broke camp at 6 a. m.
notes: Same entry as Rice's: arrival about 3 p. m., departure at 5 o'clock (conflict C-HANOVER-1JUL).

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

tier_basis: The print has "la. m." where Rice's report (R195) prints "1 a. m. [July 2]" for the same entry; the hour is read as 1 a. m. on that second witness (DD-LIFE-04).
quote: arrived within 3 miles of Gettysburg at la. m., where we bivouacked.
context_quote: July 1. — Broke camp at 6 a. m.
notes: Conflict C-BIVOUAC-1JUL (hour and distance of the bivouac of 1-2 July).

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

window.part_of_day: from the start at 4 a. m. to the order at about 4 p. m.
window.note: "Started at 4 a. m." and "awaiting orders until about 4 p. m.": the two stated clocks; the print has "lay m position"

place.text: first about 2 miles from the bivouac (a position taken up), then across the creek (Rock Creek), awaiting orders

quote: Started at 4 a. m. ; went about 2 miles, when we got into position; remained some two hours, then, crossed the creek and lay m position awaiting orders until about 4 p. m.
context_quote: July 2. — Started at 4 a. m.
notes: The 83rd's own statement of the day of waiting; Woodward, commanding the same regiment, has it "ordered into position" at about 2.30 p. m. and attacked at 3.15 p. m. (conflict C-LRT-ARRIVAL-0702).

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

window.part_of_day: during the night
window.note: "that night" after the fight of 2 July: from sunset to sunrise by the project ephemeris

place.text: on the field of the fight, Little Round Top

quote: held that position, and bivouacked on the field that night.
context_quote: July 2. — Started at 4 a. m.
notes: Same words as Rice's itinerary, which has "on the* field". Woodward: at 1.30 a. m. on the 3d the regiment moved to the support of the 20th Maine on the hill to the left.

unit_text: the regiment (the Eighty-third Pennsylvania, Maj. Lamont)

window.part_of_day: the night of 2-3 July, until about 9 a. m.
window.note: after the fight of 2 July (sunset 19:32 by the project ephemeris) until "about 9 a. m." on the 3d

place.text: the field of the previous day's fight on Little Round Top

tier_basis: The entry says the regiment "Remained on the field of the previous day's fight until about 9 a. m."; the night between is reasoned from it. Woodward, who commanded the same regiment, has it moving at 1.30 a. m. to the support of the 20th Maine and relieved at 10 a. m. by a Pennsylvania Reserves regiment.
quote: July 3. — Remained on the field of the previous day's fight until about 9 a. m., when we were relieved by the First Brigade and Ninth Massachusetts, of Second Brigade
notes: Relief hour and relieving units differ in the reports of the brigade (conflict C-RELIEF-0703).
